_readme: ADR-0904. A CEILING BOUNDS SPEND. IT NEVER REPORTS IT. Every figure here is a hand-authored worst case per invocation, used only by ADR-0909's K-group reservation. None of it may ever appear in a run.completed payload, a scorecard cost column or a proposal row -- those carry only what a driver actually reported, and an unreported cost is ABSENT, never zero and never this number. A driver+model pair with no entry is REFUSED, not defaulted: a default ceiling is a number nobody measured doing the work of a bound, and it errs in the unrecoverable direction.
_arithmetic: Re-checked 2026-08-17, when the first REAL pairs were added. commit-msg-draft is the only class clearing the fixture floor; it declares 6 fixtures of which 5 are posable (basic.json declares no repo_state, so the case cannot be posed and bench does not select it). 5 x K=3 = 15 invocations per run. THE REAL EVENT IS TWO RUNS, NOT ONE: a proposal is a COMPARISON, and `evaluateGates` refuses one whose cost is reported on a single side, so a real candidate cannot be judged against a mock champion (measured -- a mock scorecard carries no cost_inr at all). Champion run: 15 x 12 = 180. Candidate run: 15 x 6 = 90. Each run carries its own remainder, so the binding constraint is the PROCESS sub-cap in the champion run, and the 500 rupee run cap never binds. Worst case for the whole event is therefore 270 rupees, and both halves are bounded independently.
_why_the_process_sub_cap_moved_to_200_on: It was 100, and at 100 the CHAMPION run could not complete: 15 invocations at a sonnet worst case of 12 needs 180, so groups 4 and 5 would have been refused, the completeness gate would have read `the CHAMPION's evidence is incomplete`, and the run would have produced NO PROPOSAL after spending real money on three fifths of it. This file already named this as the change to make -- see _when_a_real_pair_is_added -- and it is made here with its date rather than by loosening the reservation rule, which is the one thing that must not move. 200 admits the champion with 20 to spare and still refuses a sixth fixture group.
_what_raising_the_sub_cap_DESTROYS: Stated because a change that moves a measurement owes an account of what it loosens, not only of what it fixes. At 100 the sub-cap bound a CHEAP pair tightly: haiku at 6 reserves 18 per group, so 100 refused the sixth group and the class could never commit more than 90. At 200 it does not bind on haiku until the TWELFTH group -- verified against admitGroup, not asserted here -- so the practical bound on a cheap pair is now the fixture count rather than the sub-cap. Nothing can spend it today (5 posable fixtures = 90 reserved), but the guard that would have caught a fixture count quietly tripling is now a fixture count away instead of one group away. The right correction if that ever matters is a per-pair sub-cap, not a lower global one, because a global number cannot be tight for a 6 and a 12 at the same time.
_why_these_numbers: Hand-authored, not measured -- there is still no pricing snapshot (ADR-0904), which is exactly why this file exists. 12 rupees is roughly 0.14 USD and 6 is roughly 0.07; at the published per-token rates for these two models both cover an invocation an order of magnitude larger than commit-msg-draft actually poses (a small git diff in, a commit message out). A ceiling errs high on purpose: it bounds the unrecoverable direction, and a ceiling set too LOW does not save money -- it refuses the later fixture groups after the earlier ones have already been paid for, which is the worst of both. sonnet is the class CHAMPION (router.yaml: commit-msg-draft -> balanced-workhorse -> claude-code: sonnet); haiku is the CANDIDATE, and ADR-0914 requires the candidate be a second model id under claude-code rather than the class champion.
_when_a_real_pair_is_added: Reserve K x worst_case against BOTH caps before the group starts. With K=3 and a 100 rupee process sub-cap, a worst case above 33.33 rupees per invocation admits at most ONE fixture group per class -- so if a real pair lands above that, the process sub-cap is what needs the reasoned change, recorded here with its date, not the reservation rule.
